question: With reference to ship recycling in India (in news, 2026), consider the following: 1) India became the world's largest ship-recycling nation in 2025 as per UNCTAD's Review of Maritime Transport. 2) The industry is concentrated mainly at Alang, Gujarat. 3) It is regulated domestically by the Recycling of Ships Act, 2019, which gives effect to the Hong Kong Convention. How many of the above are correct?
explanation: UNCTAD's 2025 Review ranked India first (35.4% global share); Alang, Gujarat is the hub; the Recycling of Ships Act, 2019 implements the Hong Kong Convention.
subject: Economy
micro_topic: Ship recycling / UNCTAD Review of Maritime Transport 2025

question: With reference to Ecologically Sensitive Areas (ESAs) of the Western Ghats, consider the following: 1) ESAs are notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. 2) The Gadgil Committee recommended a larger ESA than the Kasturirangan Committee. 3) The Western Ghats run through six states from Gujarat to Tamil Nadu. Which are correct?
explanation: ESAs are notified under EPA 1986; Gadgil/WGEEP proposed ~1.29 lakh sq km (100%) vs Kasturirangan's ~37%; the Ghats span six states (Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu).
subject: Environment
micro_topic: Western Ghats ESA; Gadgil vs Kasturirangan

question: The Supreme Court's 2026 ruling in Maniyar Iliyaz v. P. Ayyappan recognised the 'Right to Walk' on safe footpaths as flowing primarily from:
explanation: The Court rooted the right in freedom of movement (Art. 19(1)(d)) and the right to life (Art. 21); Article 32 was used only to re-register the matter suo motu, not as the source of the right.
subject: Polity & Governance
theme: Fundamental Rights & judicial expansion of Article 21
micro_topic: Right to walk / safe footpaths judgment

question: Fibre-optic drones, recently in the news, are valued in modern warfare mainly because they:
options: (b) Are resistant to radiofrequency jamming and spoofing
explanation: They are controlled via a physical fibre-optic cable and emit minimal RF, making them immune to jamming/spoofing; the trade-off is limited range and a cable vulnerable to breakage.
subject: Science & Technology

question: Rakhigarhi, in news for transfer of skeletal remains to the Anthropological Survey of India, is associated with which civilisation and state?
explanation: Rakhigarhi (Haryana) is among the largest Indus-Saraswati (Harappan) settlements; ASI transferred skeletal remains to AnSI's repository in Kolkata under a Ministry of Culture MoU for ancient-DNA study.
subject: Ancient & Medieval History

question: India is home to part of which of the world's biodiversity hotspots? 1) The Himalaya 2) Indo-Burma 3) Sundaland 4) Western Ghats-Sri Lanka. How many of the above are correct?
explanation: India hosts four of the 36 global biodiversity hotspots: the Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Sundaland (Nicobar Islands), and Western Ghats-Sri Lanka.
subject: Environment

question: The Western Ghats are called the 'Water Tower of Peninsular India.' Which of the following rivers rise in the Western Ghats? 1) Godavari 2) Krishna 3) Cauvery 4) Mahanadi
explanation: The Godavari (Trimbak), Krishna (Mahabaleshwar) and Cauvery (Talakaveri/Brahmagiri) rise in the Western Ghats; the Mahanadi rises in Chhattisgarh, not the Western Ghats.
subject: Geography
micro_topic: East-flowing rivers originating in the Western Ghats
